correctness.rationale: Direct beta integral gives exact pool-negative probability; first differences factor through H_k-1 and H consecutive ratios have linear sign 2beta+(1-alpha)k. F consecutive ratios have sign beta+(1-alpha)k. Gamma-ratio asymptotics prove the boundary cases alpha<=1, and integer monotonicity gives exact maximum at K for alpha>1. Exact rational H4,H5,H28,H29 prove two crossings in the beta(3/2,5/2) witness and C5<1. check_exact.py independently sums beta-binomial masses and tests 14,520 rational identities; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Lendle et al. 2011 treats correlated case identification; Basso et al. 2021 derives precisely the beta-binomial pool efficiency and compares optimal pool size against the independent model, including Propositions 1 and 2; Landolfi and Lall 2023 treats arbitrary exchangeable partitions algorithmically. The present additional claim is the all-integer beta-shape pooling-benefit criterion, exact sign-sequence classification and attained double-turn example, not the known cost formula or generic partition algorithm. The checked sections did not state or imply the complete double-turn classification, though inaccessible full text and undiscovered specialists remain risks.

value.rationale: Whether correlated specimen pooling saves scarce infectious-disease screening tests is a genuine medical resource question. A single-integer feasibility test for the beta regime and a proof that cost can turn down-up-down warn against assuming global unimodality. The exact witness uses small rational shape parameters and pool size five for its unique global optimum; no arbitrary numeric subcase is needed for the universal theorem.
